issues.description: The UML/problem statement specifies Farm.singFarmSongVerse(animal) as a private helper, but the reference solution implements it as protected. This mismatch can confuse students about required visibility and may cause them to follow the solution style while tests expect the UML-specified private visibility (or vice versa).
issues.suggestedFix: Align visibility across artifacts: change the solution's singFarmSongVerse to private (and keep template's helper private), or update the UML/problem statement to state protected if that is intended.

issues.description: The template declares singFarmSongVerse with no parameter (commented placeholder /*Animal animal*/), while the problem statement and solution require singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal). This can mislead students into implementing a parameterless helper and then struggle to iterate verses per animal as required.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template method signature to `private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)` (including importing/creating Animal as needed) and adjust its body placeholders accordingly.

issues.description: The helper method for printing a single song verse is specified as private in the problem statement/UML (singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal):void), but the solution implements it as protected. This inconsistent access modifier changes how students conceptualize the method’s intended visibility and may confuse them when aligning their implementation with the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the visibility with the UML by making singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) private in the solution (and instruct students to implement it as private).
